title: Soft Tissue Sarcoma Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Structural pathway for soft tissue sarcoma: presentation (extremity/trunk, retroperitoneal/intra-abdominal, advanced/metastatic) -> workup -> grade/size/depth risk stratification -> surgery +/- radiation +/- doxorubicin-based systemic therapy -> surveillance -> recurrence / histology-directed metastatic therapy. Treatment leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id where one clinically fits; agents/modalities without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. No proprietary guideline text is reproduced and no dose/regimen is invented. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Soft Tissue Sarcoma; regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Adjuvant/neoadjuvant radiation lowers local recurrence for high-grade or deep tumors and after close/positive margins; it does not clearly improve overall survival. Preoperative RT uses a smaller field/lower dose but has more acute wound complications than postoperative RT.

b.text: Perioperative doxorubicin-based chemotherapy in localized high-risk extremity/trunk sarcoma has an inconsistent survival benefit and is an individualized decision, weighed against anthracycline toxicity; favored for large (>5 cm), deep, high-grade tumors and chemosensitive histologies.

c.text: Retroperitoneal sarcoma is best treated by complete en-bloc resection of the tumor with adherent organs at a high-volume center; routine adjuvant chemotherapy is not standard and radiation is selective/investigational.

d.text: Surveillance intensity tracks grade: high-grade tumors need more frequent cross-sectional imaging of the primary site and chest (the lung is the dominant site of distant spread) than low-grade tumors.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Soft tissue sarcoma: presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by anatomic presentation. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Extremity or superficial trunk / body-wall mass
Retroperitoneal or intra-abdominal mass
Advanced / metastatic disease at presentation

nodes.name: Extremity workup
nodes.title: Extremity / trunk: workup
nodes.description: Image and biopsy before any resection so the tumor is staged and the biopsy tract can be excised en-bloc.
bullets: History and physical; measure tumor size and note depth relative to fascia
MRI of the primary site with contrast (CT if MRI contraindicated)
Core-needle biopsy (image-guided) before resection; place the tract so it can be excised at surgery - avoid excisional biopsy of an undiagnosed mass
Expert sarcoma pathology review: histologic type, grade (e.g. FNCLCC), margins
Chest CT to screen for pulmonary metastases; consider PET in selected cases
Multidisciplinary sarcoma-center referral before definitive treatment

nodes.name: Grade / size risk
nodes.title: Extremity / trunk: grade, size and resectability
nodes.description: Stratify by histologic grade, tumor size and depth, and whether a limb-sparing complete resection is feasible. This drives whether radiation and systemic therapy are added to surgery.

options.label: Locally advanced / not resectable with a functional limb

tables.title: Simplified extremity STS risk (grade x size/depth)

nodes.name: Low-risk extremity
nodes.title: Low-grade / small superficial: surgery
nodes.description: Wide local excision alone is usually sufficient; radiation only for margin concerns.
bullets: Wide local excision to negative margins (limb-sparing)
Adjuvant radiation generally not needed for small low-grade tumors resected with wide margins
Consider radiation for a positive margin that cannot be re-excised
No systemic therapy
Then surveillance

nodes.name: High-grade small
nodes.title: High-grade, small (<= 5 cm): surgery +/- RT
nodes.description: Limb-sparing wide excision with radiation added for close margins or deep high-grade tumors; routine chemotherapy is not indicated.
bullets: Limb-sparing wide local excision to negative margins
Adjuvant (or neoadjuvant) radiation for deep high-grade tumors or close/positive margins
Radiation may be omitted for a small high-grade tumor widely excised with a generous margin
Routine perioperative chemotherapy not indicated at this size
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Sequencing (large HG)
nodes.title: High-grade, large (> 5 cm): treatment sequencing
nodes.description: For large deep high-grade tumors, choose preoperative therapy (to shrink/facilitate limb-sparing surgery and treat micrometastatic risk) versus upfront resection.

options.label: Preoperative RT +/- doxorubicin-based chemo, then surgery
Upfront wide excision, then adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant extremity
nodes.title: High-grade large: preoperative RT +/- chemo, then surgery
nodes.description: Preoperative radiation (and, for selected high-risk chemosensitive tumors, doxorubicin-based chemotherapy), then limb-sparing resection.
bullets: Preoperative radiation to reduce local recurrence and facilitate limb-sparing surgery
Consider preoperative doxorubicin-based chemotherapy for large, deep, high-grade chemosensitive tumors (individualized)
Then limb-sparing wide local excision to negative margins; re-image response before surgery
Watch for postoperative wound-healing complications after preoperative RT
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below (dose engine computes the patient dose)
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Post-resection margin
nodes.title: After upfront resection: margin status
nodes.description: Adjuvant therapy after upfront wide excision is guided by the final surgical margin (and grade/size).

nodes.name: Upfront R0
nodes.title: Upfront resection, wide negative margin
nodes.description: Adjuvant radiation for high-grade/deep tumors; chemotherapy individualized.
bullets: Adjuvant radiation to the tumor bed for a large / deep high-grade tumor to reduce local recurrence
Consider adjuvant doxorubicin-based chemotherapy for high-risk chemosensitive tumors (individualized decision)
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Upfront close/positive
nodes.title: Upfront resection, close / positive margin
nodes.description: Re-resect if feasible; otherwise adjuvant radiation, plus individualized chemotherapy.
bullets: Re-excision to a negative margin when anatomically feasible
Adjuvant radiation to the tumor bed if re-excision is not possible or the margin remains close
Consider adjuvant doxorubicin-based chemotherapy for high-grade chemosensitive tumors (individualized)
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Unresectable extremity
nodes.title: Locally advanced / not limb-sparing resectable
nodes.description: Downstage with preoperative therapy to try to convert to limb-sparing surgery; amputation reserved for tumors not otherwise controllable.
bullets: Preoperative radiation and/or doxorubicin-based chemotherapy to attempt downstaging to a limb-sparing resection
Consider regional approaches (e.g. isolated limb perfusion) at experienced centers
Amputation reserved for tumors not controllable with limb-sparing therapy or with major neurovascular involvement
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below
Then surveillance if rendered resectable

nodes.name: Retroperitoneal workup
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal / intra-abdominal: workup
nodes.description: Characterize the mass and its organ relationships before an operative plan; percutaneous biopsy is selective.
bullets: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast (+/- MRI) to map organ and vascular involvement
Image-guided core biopsy when it will change management (e.g. suspected lymphoma, germ-cell tumor, or planned preoperative therapy); a percutaneous coaxial approach is preferred
Expert pathology review - well-differentiated vs dedifferentiated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma are the common subtypes
Assess resectability and organs likely resected en-bloc; high-volume sarcoma center referral

nodes.name: RP resectability
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal: resectability
nodes.description: The single most important determinant of outcome is a complete en-bloc resection at the first operation.

nodes.name: RP resectable
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal, resectable: en-bloc resection
nodes.description: Complete en-bloc resection with adherent organs; radiation selective, chemotherapy not standard.
bullets: Complete en-bloc resection of the tumor with involved/adherent organs, aiming for a macroscopically complete (R0/R1) resection at the first operation
Preoperative radiation is selective / investigational and not routine; discuss at a sarcoma multidisciplinary meeting
Adjuvant chemotherapy is not standard for resected retroperitoneal sarcoma
Then surveillance (dedifferentiated liposarcoma and high-grade tumors recur locally)

nodes.name: RP unresectable
nodes.title: Retroperitoneal, unresectable / metastatic
nodes.description: Consider preoperative therapy to convert to resectable; otherwise histology-directed systemic therapy / palliation.
bullets: Preoperative doxorubicin-based chemotherapy and/or radiation to attempt conversion to a resectable tumor in a fit patient
If still unresectable or metastatic, treat by histology (see the histology-directed systemic pathway)
Palliative measures for obstruction / pain / bleeding as needed

nodes.name: Metastatic workup
nodes.title: Advanced / metastatic: workup
nodes.description: Confirm histology and extent, then decide whether disease is oligometastatic (amenable to local therapy) or disseminated.
bullets: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis to map metastatic sites (lung is the dominant site)
Confirm histologic subtype and grade on biopsy; expert pathology review
Assess whether metastases are limited/resectable (oligometastatic) vs widespread
Assess performance status, organ function and cardiac reserve before anthracycline therapy

nodes.name: Fitness
nodes.title: Advanced disease: fitness for systemic therapy
nodes.description: Match intensity of therapy to performance status and organ function.

nodes.name: Best supportive care
nodes.title: Unfit: best supportive / palliative care
nodes.description: Symptom-directed care with palliative local therapy where useful.
bullets: Best supportive / palliative care with early palliative-care involvement
Palliative radiation or surgery for local symptoms (pain, bleeding, cord/organ compression)
Consider a gentle single-agent or reduced-intensity regimen only if performance status improves

nodes.name: Histology-directed
nodes.title: Advanced STS: histology-directed systemic therapy
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for advanced STS is directed by histologic subtype; oligometastatic disease may instead be treated with local therapy.

nodes.name: LMS line
nodes.title: Leiomyosarcoma: line of therapy
nodes.description: Choose first-line versus later-line therapy for advanced leiomyosarcoma.

nodes.name: LMS 1st line
nodes.title: Leiomyosarcoma: first line
nodes.description: Anthracycline-based therapy; gemcitabine + docetaxel is an active alternative.
bullets: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy (single-agent or doxorubicin-containing combination)
Gemcitabine + docetaxel is an active alternative first-line combination for leiomyosarcoma
Regimens referenced below (dose engine computes the patient dose)

nodes.name: LMS later line
nodes.title: Leiomyosarcoma: later line
nodes.description: Gemcitabine + docetaxel if not used first line; then trabectedin or pazopanib.
bullets: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (if not used first line)
Then trabectedin, pazopanib, or dacarbazine-based therapy (guidance where no dose protocol exists here)
Gemcitabine + docetaxel regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Liposarcoma subtype
nodes.title: Liposarcoma: subtype
nodes.description: Systemic sensitivity differs by liposarcoma subtype.

nodes.name: Liposarcoma WD/DD
nodes.title: Well-differentiated / dedifferentiated liposarcoma
nodes.description: Doxorubicin-based first line; trabectedin/eribulin later.
bullets: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy first line
Trabectedin or eribulin at later lines (guidance where no dose protocol exists here)
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Liposarcoma myxoid
nodes.title: Myxoid / round-cell liposarcoma
nodes.description: Doxorubicin-based first line; particularly sensitive to trabectedin.
bullets: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy first line
Myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma is notably sensitive to trabectedin (and to radiation) at later lines
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Angiosarcoma
nodes.title: Angiosarcoma: taxane-based
nodes.description: Angiosarcoma is uniquely taxane-sensitive; doxorubicin is an alternative.
bullets: Taxane (paclitaxel) is preferred first line - angiosarcoma is uniquely taxane-sensitive (no dedicated dose protocol here yet - guidance)
Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy is an active alternative
Consider anti-angiogenic therapy at later lines

nodes.name: Synovial / spindle
nodes.title: Synovial / other spindle-cell sarcoma
nodes.description: Doxorubicin +/- ifosfamide; these histologies are relatively chemosensitive.
bullets: Doxorubicin +/- ifosfamide (synovial sarcoma is relatively chemosensitive)
High-dose ifosfamide or pazopanib at later lines (guidance where no dose protocol exists here)
Doxorubicin-based regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Oligometastatic
nodes.title: Oligometastatic: local therapy
nodes.description: Limited resectable metastases (typically lung) can be treated with local therapy with curative intent in selected patients.
bullets: Metastasectomy (e.g. pulmonary metastasectomy) for resectable, limited disease in a fit patient
Stereotactic body radiation as a local option for unresectable oligometastases
Consider peri-procedural histology-directed systemic therapy
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy; intensity tracks tumor grade.
bullets: High-grade: history/physical + primary-site and chest imaging every 3-6 months for 2-3 years, then 6-monthly to 5 years, then annually
Low-grade: less frequent (e.g. 6-12 monthly) clinical and imaging follow-up
Cross-sectional imaging of the primary site (MRI extremity / CT retroperitoneum); chest CT or radiograph for pulmonary metastases
Educate the patient on new mass, pain, or pulmonary symptoms between visits
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: local vs distant
nodes.description: Distinguish isolated local recurrence (potentially still curable) from distant metastatic recurrence.
bullets: Biopsy / re-image to confirm recurrence and restage (chest CT for distant disease)
Expert re-review of histology and grade

nodes.name: Local recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated local recurrence: re-resection
nodes.description: Treated with curative intent - re-resection and radiation if not previously given.
bullets: Re-resection to negative margins when feasible (limb-sparing if possible)
Radiation to the recurrence bed if not previously delivered
Amputation only if limb-sparing control is not achievable
Consider histology-directed systemic therapy for high-grade / rapidly recurrent disease
